(Tillu @ Sanjay Rathore Vs The State Of Madhya Prade
 Dated : 04-11-2025
Ms. Durgesh Gupta - Advocate for the appellant.

Shri Arvind Singh - Public Prosecutor for the responden
Heard on I.A.No.25173 of 2022, which is the first application under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C. for
suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.

This appeal has been preferred against the judgment dated 13.01.2022 passed by Special Judge,
POCSO Act, 2012 and SC/ST (PoA) Act, 1989, Hosangabad, District Hoshangabad (M.P.) in Special Case No.51 of 2020, whereby appellant has been convicted and sentenced as under:
Conviction U/s. Imprisonment Fine
In lieu of default fine 376(3) of IPC Imprisonment for Life Rs.2,000/- R.I. for 02 months Learned counsel for the appellant submits that he is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that there was a previous enmity parents of the prosecutrix with appellant and therefore, false and fabricated complaint was lodged against the appellant.
There are contradictions and omissions in the statements of the prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161 and 164 of the Cr.P.C.
As per the medical report, no internal or external injury was found on the body of the prosecutrix.
The appellant is in jail since 27.11.2019 and has already undergone more than 06 years of incarceration.
This appeal is of the year 2022 and there is no possibility of early hearing of the appeal in near future.
He is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by the directions and conditions, which may be imposed by this Court.
Hence, it is prayed that the application for suspension of sentence may be allowed.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the application and supported the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence passed by the trial court.
He further submits that at the time of the incident, prosecutrix was a minor aged about 14 years 07 months and DNA report is also positive therefore, prays for rejection of the bail application.

Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties and looking to the overall facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the opinion that the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant can be considered.

sentences.text: Accordingly, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the aforesaid I.A. is allowed.

It is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, the remaining jail sentence of the appellant is hereby suspended and he be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this Court on 17 .02.2026 and on such other dates, as may be fixed by the Registry in this regard during pendency of this appeal.
List the matter for final hearing in due course.

(VIVEK KUMAR SINGH) (H  JUDGE   SSL Tillu @ Sanjay Rathore vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151798036/
